searchText: I've been noticing CPU load increasing over the past week(s), I assume due to increased validator registry size. I think on average the CPU load increase may really be as you say the size of the network, but there's a correlation of bad votes with days of high volume of transactions of ETH1, so I can only assume that are the CPU localized spikes of geth that are causing this, on both ends proposing and attesting. So I'm only referring to short term spikes. This suggests that users might find value in using `nice` to give priority to eth2 clients over eth1 clients. If the only reason they're using eth1 is to support eth1, it's totally fine if the eth1 node is lagging behind by a matter of hours. Not a long term solution, but an interesting consideration for those looking to really maximise staking rewards. That's a good tip! From a mnemonic so that I can check the address displayed by ledger is correct, given we don't have access to the ledger code. https://github.com/wealdtech/ethdo/blob/master/docs/conversions.md Been taking a look at the proportion of correct head votes across the network. The decline is pretty clear, and on-going. Methodology: - find all the attestations that occurred for slots in an epoch - for each validator in the attestation: - add 1 to total - add 1 to correct head if the attestation contains the correct head vote Then you calculate correct head / total to find out the proportion of correct head votes. Are you counting twice the same attestations or just the first time it's included. I desisted of doing this before patching chaind to count votes for blocks Just the first time. (Advanced reporting out of chaind data is an entirely different beast, I've been playing around with various methodologies to do it and ended up with a kind-of reporting pipeline, but it's pretty rough and ready at the moment) This is a pretty basic question, so feel free to refer me elsewhere if it's the wrong channel, but are ETH 2.0 rewards from staking a result of fees paid for transactions, or from minting new ETH? Rewards are minted ETH. PoS also has a fee burning mechanism in place, but it operates independently of the minted rewards. eth2 call in 40 minutes https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-pm/issues/203 One of my alerts is excatly that an incorrect head vote. The past couple weeks I’ve been getting these alerts constantly whereas before I didn’t at all. I thought it was a network or load issue but it isn’t so perhaps that coincides with your stats there Ie this now happens a lot more regularly unlike before Why does this happen does anyone know? Quick notes from me: https://hackmd.io/@benjaminion/H1p6GhG-d (I had to go back and listen again to the Upgrade section: lots of info. Hopefully reasonably summarised, but listen to the recording if in doubt.)
